title: Finite tangent and infinitesimal automorphism spaces of coherent families
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $f:X\to B$ be a finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For an $S$-scheme $T$, let $\mathcal C(T)$ be the groupoid of pairs $(b:T\to B,M)$, where $M$ is a finitely presented quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{X\times_BT}$-module, flat over $T$, with support proper over $T$. Here finite presentation means etale locally a cokernel of a map between finite rank free modules; flatness is stalkwise flatness over base local rings on etale charts [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]; proper support means $M\simeq i_*N$ for a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X\times_BT$ with $Z\to T$ proper and $N$ finite type quasi-coherent [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. Modules and tensor pullback use [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module, def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Arrows over $v:T\to T_1$ are isomorphisms $v_X^*M_1\simeq M$ with $b=b_1v$; composition uses canonical pullback composition isomorphisms. Assume $S$ is locally Noetherian (it has an affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]) and $B\to S$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. For every field $k$ with a finite type map $\operatorname{Spec}k\to S$ and every $x_0\in\mathcal C(k)$, the following two $k$-vector spaces are finite dimensional: the tangent space of isomorphism classes of pairs $(x,\alpha)$ with $x\in\mathcal C(k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))$ and $\alpha:x|_k\simeq x_0$, and the infinitesimal automorphism space of automorphisms of the pullback of $x_0$ to $k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ which restrict to the identity over $k$. Vector-space operations are the usual deformation operations induced by scalar multiplication of $\epsilon$ and gluing first-order extensions along their common special fibre [def-weil-field, def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

proof.text: Let $s$ be the image of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ in $S$ and choose an affine Noetherian neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $s$. Every $\operatorname{Spec}(k\oplus V)$ for finite-dimensional $V$ has the same single underlying point as $\operatorname{Spec}k$, hence every deformation test map factors uniquely through $U$. Restrict $B$ and $X$ to $U$. This changes neither objects, markings, arrows nor any scalar or addition operation under consideration. The local finite-presentation hypotheses are unchanged on this open restriction, and $k$ is a finite type $R$-algebra. We may therefore work over $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$.

Local finite presentation on spaces is stable under base change: take etale scheme charts of source and target, tensor each chart presentation $A[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/(h_1,\ldots,h_m)$ with the new affine base ring, and use [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition] and [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test]. The base-changed charts cover by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]; [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties] permits etale chart refinement. Consequently $X_0=X\times_{B,b_0}\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite presentation. It is also quasi-compact and quasi-separated: each affine test of it, or of its relative diagonal, is the corresponding base-change test for $f$, or for its diagonal. Thus $X_0/k$ is of finite presentation, with the convention of [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. Also every $B\times_ST\to T$ is locally of finite presentation. Apply [lem-sfb-stack-representable-source-algebraic] to $B\to S$, viewing the scheme $S$ as an algebraic stack with identity atlas. Its base changes are algebraic spaces, so $B$ is an algebraic stack locally of finite presentation over $S$, meaning it admits a smooth surjective scheme atlas locally finitely presented over $S$. That atlas is locally of finite type because each ring presentation has finitely many generators. Thus [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-tangent-finite] gives a finite-dimensional space $T_{b_0}B$ of $S$-maps $\operatorname{Spec}(k[\epsilon])\to B$ extending $b_0$. This is a set of maps, with no nonidentity automorphisms.

source.place: Tag 08W8, reduction to the fixed fibre; artin.tex Tag 07X1 (lemma-finite-dimension).

proof.text: For $A_1\to A\leftarrow A_2$ in the test category with $A_2\to A$ surjective, the kernel is nilpotent, so $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}A_2$ is a thickening, and $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}A_1$ is affine. By [lem-sfb-scheme-affine-thickening-pushout] the scheme pushout $P$ exists and $\operatorname{Spec}A_1\to P$ is a thickening, hence a homeomorphism; thus $P$ has one point, and its nonempty affine open is all of $P$. Taking $X,Y$ to be the identities in [lem-sfb-infinitesimal-pushout-affine-charts], with $P_0=P$, the canonical map identifies $P$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(A_1\times_AA_2)$. So [lem-sfb-space-coherent-pushout] applies to these spectra of Artinian ring fibre products; retain the special-fibre marking. The resulting equivalence remains fully faithful and essentially surjective after marking: an isomorphism of restrictions induces precisely the same identification with $x_0$. It gives (RS) for the marked predeformation category over $R$ of [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category]. Its fibre over $k$ has one object up to a unique marked arrow. Hence [lem-sfb-artin-rs-tangent-tensor] makes its tangent set $T$ a $k$-vector space. Apply the same statements with base $\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the morphism $X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: its coherent-family tangent space $T_0$ is a vector space as well. The ring fibre product $k[\epsilon]\times_k k[\epsilon]$ is $k\oplus k^2$, with square-zero ideal $k^2$; the sum map is $(a,b,c)\mapsto a+(b+c)\epsilon$. Thus these vector operations are exactly the scalar pullbacks and gluing operations in the item.

source.place: Tag 08W8, first paragraph, with quot.tex Tag 08LQ and formal-defos.tex Tag 06IH.

proof.text: Forgetting the module defines $d:T\to T_{b_0}B$. It preserves scalar multiplication by functorial pullback. It preserves addition because the glued pair has the unique base map restricting to the two given base maps, and both sums pull it back along the same map $k\oplus k^2\to k[\epsilon]$. This uniqueness follows directly from [lem-sfb-space-coherent-pushout]: apply it to the identity morphism $B\to B$ and the two zero modules. Prescribed compatible base maps then glue uniquely, since the zero module has only its identity isomorphism. A class lies in $\ker d$ exactly when its base map is the constant lift $b_0\circ(\operatorname{Spec}(k[\epsilon])\to\operatorname{Spec}k)$. For that map the source is canonically $X_0\times_k\operatorname{Spec}(k[\epsilon])$, and its module, marking and arrows are precisely a marked object for $X_0/k$. Thus $T_0\to T$ is injective and identifies $T_0$ with $\ker d$; there are no extra base isomorphisms because $B$ is set-valued. This map is $k$-linear. On $k[\epsilon]$ and $k\oplus k^2$, with their $k$-algebra structures, it keeps the module and replaces the structure map by its composite with $b_0$, and it commutes with pullback along $k$-algebra maps. Scalar multiplication is such a pullback. A glued object over $k\oplus k^2$ for $X_0/k$ is sent to an object with the two given restrictions. By the uniqueness in (RS) from step 3, it is the gluing used for the sum in $T$. Both sums then pull back along the same map $k\oplus k^2\to k[\epsilon]$.

source.place: Tag 08W8, reduction paragraph; direct kernel calculation of the special case of artin.tex Tag 07X2.

proof.text: Write $M_0$ for the module in $x_0$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-proper-support-module-ext-finite] to $X_0/k$ and $M=N=M_0$. Step 2 supplies local finite presentation of $X_0/k$. The other hypotheses are exactly the finite-presentation, quasi-coherence and proper-support hypotheses on the given object $x_0$: the closed proper subspace is the one in its proper-support datum. We obtain finite-dimensional vector spaces $E^1=\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal O_{X_0}}(M_0,M_0)$ and $E^0=\operatorname{Ext}^0_{\mathcal O_{X_0}}(M_0,M_0)$. Properness of $X_0$ is not used.

source.place: Tag 08W8, final paragraph; proper-support repair using spaces-perfect.tex Tags 0D0S and 0D0R.

proof.text: Forget finite presentation, quasi-coherence and proper support in a marked fixed-base deformation. This is a full inclusion into the groupoid of all module lifts on $X_0\times_k\operatorname{Spec}(k[\epsilon])$ flat over $k[\epsilon]$: both categories have all module isomorphisms commuting with the marking. The chart flatness agrees with geometric-stalk flatness by [lem-sfb-space-module-flat-chart-test]. By [lem-sfb-space-module-split-deformation-ext], forgetting gives an injection $j:T_0\hookrightarrow E^1$. It preserves zero since both origins are the trivial module lift, and scalars since both operations use the same base pullback. For addition, the coherent gluing of [lem-sfb-space-coherent-pushout] becomes a gluing in all flat modules; uniqueness of that gluing in [lem-sfb-space-module-split-deformation-ext] identifies it with the ambient sum. Hence $j$ is linear. It is unnecessary to assert that every flat lift has finite presentation or proper support.

source.place: Tag 08W8, fixed-fibre module deformation paragraph, using defos.tex Tag 08VW; full inclusion suffices instead of Tag 08W7.

proof.text: The infinitesimal automorphisms in the item are exactly the marked automorphisms of the trivial module lift in step 6. The base map of that object is fixed, and an algebraic space has no nonidentity base automorphisms. Removing the conditions on objects does not change automorphisms of this same object. Thus [lem-sfb-space-module-split-deformation-ext] identifies this space with $E^0$, respecting composition as addition and scalar pullback. It is finite dimensional by step 5.

source.place: Tag 08W8, displayed Ext^0 formula; defos.tex Tag 08VW(3).

proof.text: The linear injection $j$ and finiteness of $E^1$ imply that $T_0$ has a finite basis: an independent list in $T_0$ maps to an independent list in $E^1$, so adjoining vectors outside the span stops after at most $\dim E^1$ steps. The image of $d$ is likewise finite dimensional inside $T_{b_0}B$. Choose a basis of $\ker d=T_0$ and lift every vector of a basis of $\operatorname{im}d$ to $T$. These finitely many vectors span $T$: subtracting the lifted image coordinates from any vector leaves an element of the kernel. Thus $\dim T\leq\dim E^1+\dim T_{b_0}B<\infty$. Step 7 gives the other finiteness assertion. Every operation used was the specified deformation operation.

proof_origin.place: Tag 08W8 (lemma-coherent-tangent-space), with the proper-support Ext argument completed using spaces-perfect.tex Tags 0D0S and 0D0R.

lean.statement: theorem coherent_tangent_finite (hfp : ProperQuotFinitePresentation f) [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (hB : ∀ U : B.EtaleSite, LocallyOfFinitePresentation U.obj.left.hom) [LocallyOfFiniteType a] [QuasiCompact a] : ∃ (_ : AddCommGroup (Tangent f a x)) (_ : Module k (Tangent f a x)), FiniteDimensional k (Tangent f a x) ∧ (∀ t : Tangent f a x, IsZeroClass f a x t ↔ t = 0) ∧ (∀ (c : k) (t s : Tangent f a x), IsScalarClass f a x c t s ↔ s = c • t) ∧ (∀ t s r : Tangent f a x, IsSumClass f a x t s r ↔ r = t + s) ∧ ∃ Y : TrivialLift f a x, ∃ (_ : AddCommGroup (InfAut f a x Y)) (_ : Module k (InfAut f a x Y)), FiniteDimensional k (InfAut f a x Y) ∧ (∀ g : InfAut f a x Y, g = 0 ↔ g.val = Iso.refl _) ∧ (∀ g h : InfAut f a x Y, (g + h).val = g.val ≪≫ h.val) ∧ ∀ (c : k) (g h : InfAut f a x Y), IsAutScalar f a x Y c g h ↔ h = c • g
